fields.name: abbrvname
fields.description: Typically, the short name of the district as recorded in official zoning documents maintained by the jurisdiction; however, if the jurisdiction does not offer an abbreviated name, either the full name of the district or an abbreviation chosen for convenience.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The full name of the district as recorded in official zoning documents maintained by the jurisdiction.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Classification of a district as primarily residential (housing is the main permitted use), mixed with residential (housing is permitted alongside commercial and other uses), nonresidential (housing is prohibited as a principal use), or overlay not affecting use (specific to overlay districts that do not affect the residential-use permissions of the underlying base district).

fields.name: nonresidential_type
fields.description: The most common nonresidential use permitted. Provided for districts classified as mixed with residential, nonresidential, or overlay not affecting use. Please review additional explanation at www.landuselabs.com/nonresidential.

fields.name: family1_treatment
fields.description: How 1-family housing—a single dwelling unit built as a principal use on an individual lot—is regulated: as-of-right, after a public hearing, prohibited (including not explicitly permitted), or overlay not affecting use (specific to overlay districts that do not affect the residential-use permissions of the underlying base district).

fields.name: family1_minlotacres
fields.description: The minimum area of land required per lot to develop 1-family housing.

fields.name: family1_minlotacres_min
fields.description: Used for answers with alternative/contextual units for which a numerical range may be ascertained, this answer includes a single number representing the lowest minimum lot size required for 1-family housing. If there is no minimum for a district, the value is NULL. See family1_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

fields.name: family1_minlotacres_max
fields.description: Used for answers with alternative/contextual units for which a numerical range may be ascertained, this answer includes a single number representing the highest minimum lot size required for 1-family housing. If there is no maximum for a district, the value is NULL. See family1_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

fields.name: family1_frontsetbackft
fields.description: The minimum distance 1-family housing must be set back from the front property line (the street-facing boundary of the lot).

fields.name: family1_sidesetbackft
fields.description: The minimum distance 1-family housing must be set back from a side property line; can differ for lots interior to a block and corner lots (i.e., for the side of the corner lot that is not the "front").

fields.name: family1_rearsetbackft
fields.description: The minimum distance 1-family housing must be set back from the rear property line.

fields.name: family1_maxlotcoverage_building
fields.description: The maximum percentage of the lot that may be covered by the footprint of 1-family buildings.

fields.name: family1_maxlotcoverage_buildingimpervious
fields.full_name: 1-Family Max. Lot Coverage Buildings & Impervious Surface (%)
fields.description: The maximum percentage of the lot that may be covered by 1-family buildings and other impervious surfaces (such as driveways or patios).

fields.name: family1_minparking
fields.description: The minimum number of off-street parking spaces required per 1-family housing unit.

fields.name: family1_maxstories
fields.description: The maximum height permitted for 1-family housing, measured in stories.

fields.name: family1_maxheightft
fields.description: The maximum height permitted for 1-family housing, measured in feet.

fields.name: family1_floorarearatio
fields.description: The maximum ratio of a 1-family building's total floor area to the area of the lot on which it sits; a measure of development intensity.

fields.name: family1_minunitsqft
fields.description: The minimum floor area required per 1-family housing unit.

fields.name: affordable_treatment
fields.description: How affordable housing is regulated: as-of-right, after a public hearing, prohibited, overlay not affecting use (specific to overlay districts that do not affect the residential-use permissions of the underlying base district), and not mentioned (i.e., not explicitly permitted).

fields.name: affordable_definition
fields.description: The definition of affordable housing, which may include provisions such as all or some units within individual developments being subject to rent caps, deed restrictions, set-asides of units, payments, or occupancy limitations. (See affordable_treatment to determine if this definition applies to all developments within a district.)

fields.name: affordable_elderly_only
fields.description: Indicates whether occupancy of one or all units of affordable housing is restricted to people over a certain age (retirement age).

fields.name: affordable_minlotacres
fields.description: The minimum area of land required per lot to develop an affordable housing development.

fields.name: affordable_minlotacres_min
fields.description: Used for answers with alternative/contextual units for which a numerical range may be ascertained, this answer includes a single number representing the lowest minimum lot size required for an affordable housing development. If there is no minimum for a district, the value is NULL. See affordable_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

If there is no maximum for a district, the value is NULL. See affordable_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

fields.name: affordable_maxunitsperbldg

fields.name: accessory_treatment
fields.description: How accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—secondary dwelling units on a lot on which a primary dwelling already exists, which may be attached to, within, or detached from the primary dwelling—are regulated: as-of-right, after a public hearing, prohibited, overlay not affecting use (specific to overlay districts that do not affect the residential-use permissions of the underlying base district), and not mentioned (i.e., not explicitly permitted).

fields.name: accessory_family_required
fields.description: Indicates whether ADU occupancy is restricted to family members and/or employees of the property owner.

fields.name: accessory_renter_prohibited
fields.description: Indicates whether ADU occupancy is restricted to non-renters (i.e., the district bans rentals on lots containing ADUs).

fields.name: accessory_owner_required
fields.description: Indicates whether the property owner must live on site. TRUE indicates that the owner must occupy either the primary dwelling or the ADU. FALSE indicates that the owner may live off-site.

fields.name: accessory_elderly_only
fields.description: Indicates whether ADU occupancy is restricted to people over a certain age (retirement age).

fields.name: accessory_minlotacres
fields.description: The minimum area of land required per lot that includes an ADU.

fields.name: accessory_minlotacres_min
fields.description: Used for answers with alternative/contextual units for which a numerical range may be ascertained, this answer includes a single number representing the lowest minimum lot size required for an ADU. If there is no minimum for a district, the value is NULL. See accessory_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

fields.name: accessory_minlotacres_max
fields.description: Used for answers with alternative/contextual units for which a numerical range may be ascertained, this answer includes a single number representing the highest minimum lot size required for an ADU. If there is no maximum for a district, the value is NULL. See accessory_minlotacres answer to determine conditions for which this number applies.

fields.name: accessory_minparking
fields.description: The minimum number of off-street parking spaces required specifically for an ADU, additional to spaces required for the principal use(s).

fields.name: accessory_primarystructure_only
fields.full_name: ADU Restricted to Only Primary Structure
fields.description: Indicates whether the ADU must be physically attached to the primary structure. TRUE indicates the ADU must be attached. FALSE indicates that the ADU may be detached (e.g., garage apartment or carriage house conversion).

fields.name: accessory_maxpercent
fields.description: The maximum size of the ADU as a percentage of the size of the principal unit.

fields.name: accessory_maxsqft
fields.description: The maximum size of the ADU in square feet.

fields.name: accessory_maxbedrooms
fields.description: The maximum number of bedrooms permitted within an ADU.

fields.name: plannedresidential_treatment
fields.description: How planned residential developments (PRDs)—comprehensively planned residential projects often subject to unified design standards and developed as a whole rather than lot by lot—are regulated: as-of-right, after a public hearing, prohibited, overlay not affecting use (specific to overlay districts that do not affect the residential-use permissions of the underlying base district), and not mentioned (i.e., not explicitly permitted).

fields.name: plannedresidential_mobilehome
fields.full_name: PRD Mobile or Manufactured Home Park
fields.description: Indicates whether a PRD may be utilized for a mobile and/or manufactured home park. TRUE indicates that the zoning code explicitly authorized PRDs for mobile and/or manufactured homes. FALSE indicates that the zoning code did not.

fields.name: plannedresidential_maxunitsperacre
fields.description: The maximum number of units per acre permitted for a PRD.

fields.name: plannedresidential_maxunits
fields.description: The maximum total number of housing units permitted within a PRD.

fields.name: plannedresidential_mindevacres
fields.description: The minimum size a piece of land must be to develop a PRD.

fields.name: affordable_district
fields.description: Indicates whether all housing developments must be designated affordable in some way, such as all or some units within individual developments being subject to rent caps, deed restrictions, set-asides of units, payments, or occupancy limitations.

fields.name: elderly_district
fields.description: Indicates whether all housing developments must be designated for people over a certain age (retirement age), such as some or all units within individual developments being restricted to "55 or older" occupancy restrictions.
